rules.text: Use project-neutral contracts and adapters; keep project-specific facts only in the task continuity payload.
The event log, validated contract, runtime policy and code handoff bundle are authoritative; external Markdown is never a runtime prerequisite.
Before retiring legacy workflow sources, preserve every non-blank line as structured local migration evidence and verify the packaged runtime policy.
Create a bounded plan and contract before dispatching execution.
Management is the user-facing role and communicates in plain language.
Execution reports technical state to management and does not redefine the user goal.
Direct ordinary user business requests are redirected to management unless they carry a validated manual relay.
Probe create, send, wait and read capabilities before choosing native collaboration; otherwise disclose manual mode and missing capabilities.
Detect migration intent around handoff or conversation transfer and obtain confirmation; ordinary continuation is not migration intent.
Install or resolve the exact Skill version in every destination and require code-generated readiness before any business handoff.
Transfer contract, event state, role policy, facts, boundaries and next action in a self-contained validated code bundle with no required external reads.
When native collaboration is unavailable, generate a user-forwardable relay that invokes the same bootstrap and code-bundle receiver and explains the manual steps.
Management waits for execution, checks intermediate state, corrects direction and independently accepts the final outcome.
Execution starts only after one event atomically binds the dispatch, message and destination identities to an acknowledged host delivery.
Every wait, observation and correction is bound to a monotonic supervision epoch; a prior epoch cannot satisfy a later review gate.
A correction continues the same dispatch and execution task with a new correction identity and evidence delta; it does not repeat execution start or create a replacement task.
Structured delegation records role, agent identities, ownership scope, access, output, dependencies and aggregator; concurrent execution writers cannot overlap scopes.
Independent acceptance is bound to the current report revision, event cursor, work state and a non-execution reviewer identity.
Host settings evidence is read-only; it can prove inheritance or a user change but never authorizes an automatic model or preference mutation.
Repeated observed progress cursors request the first fault, blocker and narrowed next action from the same execution task; timeouts are not progress evidence.
A checkpoint, report or local fake is not final acceptance.
A repair completes only after the original failure, first faulty production layer, shared root-cause fix, red-green regression and direct consumers are proven.
Recovery of already affected state is tracked separately and can never substitute for product root-cause closure.
When recovery is required, validate an isolated production-chain candidate, rebind current identities, rerun shared validators, and require snapshot-first zero-write guarded mutation for real data.
Acceptance requires configured non-target conservation scopes and any configured external-call ledger to remain accounted for.
After destination readiness, code handoff acceptance and management confirmation, remove the exact source task by delete or archive only when user-authorized.
Place Skill artifacts under one controlled project-local root with contracts, state, reports, handoffs, evidence and temporary data separated.
After accepted completion or handoff, retain current and previous generations and remove only registered older Skill-owned artifacts after a dry run.
Do not delete or overwrite user data, credentials, configuration, sessions, dependencies, Git objects or unregistered files through artifact retention.
Redact credentials before writing contracts, events, reports, handoffs or public artifacts.
Collect all defects found in one continuous user request into one release batch and publish one version after the batch passes.
Bump patch for compatible fixes, minor for backward-compatible capabilities and major only with explicit user authorization.
